problem_type: Finite-horizon single-supplier, single-product, homogeneous limited-fleet Production Inventory Routing Problem (partial replenishment allowed, stockouts forbidden)

decisions.business: Visiting route of each vehicle in each period; a route lists location numbers in actual travel order, with the supplier numbered 0 and customers numbered 1,…,N.
decisions.shape: list[list[list[int]]], shape H×M×variable route length; routes[t][k] is the route of vehicle k in period t, an unused vehicle is denoted by the empty list [], and a used route must have the form [0,customers…,0].
decisions.completeness: Exactly M vehicle slots must be provided for every period. Each non-empty route may contain supplier 0 only at its start and end, must contain at least one customer, and its customers must not form a subtour detached from the supplier; the same customer appears at most once across all routes in the same period.

decisions.business: Quantity of product loaded and actually delivered by each vehicle to each customer in each period, corresponding to q_ikt in the model.
decisions.shape: list[list[list[float]]], fixed shape H×M×N; deliveries[t][k][i-1] is the delivery quantity from vehicle k to customer i in period t.
decisions.completeness: One nonnegative number must be provided for every period, vehicle, and customer. The delivery quantity must be 0 when the customer is not on the corresponding vehicle route; all delivery quantities of an unused vehicle must be 0. The total delivery of each vehicle in each period must not exceed vehicle_capacity, and the customer inventory after delivery must not exceed capacity and must be sufficient to cover the current-period demand. Visiting a customer does not require a positive delivery quantity, nor does it require filling up the inventory.

decisions.business: Inventory of the supplier and all customers at the end of each period; customer inventory is counted after the current-period delivery and demand are completed, and supplier inventory is counted after the current-period production and vehicle loading are completed.
decisions.shape: list[list[float]], fixed shape H×(N+1); end_inventory[t][0] is the supplier's end-of-period-t inventory, end_inventory[t][i] is the end-of-period-t inventory of customer i.
decisions.completeness: Must cover all periods and all locations, and must balance exactly period by period with initial_inventory, supplier_production, customer_demand, and deliveries. The supplier's end-of-period inventory must lie within its capacity; for each customer, the previous end-of-period inventory plus the total current-period delivery must lie between the current-period demand and the customer capacity, so the customer end-of-period inventory must not be negative.
